items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: He found the dates that I give him were correct.

ctx.x: They would come in and listen to you.

Yes. Sit up in the lobby. They wasn't working. They'd sit up there and listen. Why would he almost cry? Well, because he was out of a job. Oh. And at that time when that music was changing and they had to have something to work that was before the record. After the record was out there, many of them came there. It's been said that many of these colored men preceded us up there. Because I don't know about that. I couldn't comment. But I can tell you one band that didn't precede us to New York. That was the Creole…
Well, Mr. Broome found the same thing in Chicago. Yes, sir.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: I have letters that I sent to this Brian Russ, and I tell him about the men who played on the recording.

ctx.x: What about Signer Running? You say he made some records.

Oh yes, he recorded with us in the latter part of our contact with the victim. The numbers offhand I can't tell you, but if you look through the files, you'll find out I have letters that I sent to this Brian Russ, and I tell him about the men who played on the recording.

After I came back to New Orleans, I laid around a little while before I'd go back into the building business, building houses and repair. I sent to Wilson Hotel, which was the same punchy trade hotel, now it's called Wilson, for my trunk. I found out it had...
